title: Count bottles into packs, and packs into cases
brief: Start runs the belt and it keeps running; Stop stops it. Count the bottles the eye sees: every 6 bottles make a pack, so the Packs display goes up by one and the Bottles display goes back to 0. When 4 packs have been made, the case is full: the belt stops by itself and Case full lights. Case removed sets both counts back to 0 and puts the light out; then Start runs the belt for the next case.
hints: Use two up counters: C1 counts bottles (PV 6), C2 counts packs (PV 4). What does C2 count? Each time C1 finishes.
C1 must start again from 0 after every pack: something has to turn on its R input when C1.Q comes on.
R takes one tag, but C1 must be cleared both when a pack is done and when Case removed is pressed: a memory tag (PackReset, say) from a branch of the two does it. The belt's seal-in stops on C2.Q.

assertions.says: Start should run the belt, and it should keep running.
Three bottles have passed the eye by 2.2 s: Bottles should show 3.
Six bottles have passed by 3.7 s: Packs should show 1.
After six bottles, the Bottles count should start again from 0.

scenarios.name: Four packs fill a case, and the belt stops

assertions.says: Seventeen bottles have passed by 9 s: that is 2 full packs (and 5 bottles), so Packs should show 2.
Seventeen bottles by 9 s: 2 packs and 5 bottles.
Only 23 bottles by 12.2 s: the case is not full yet.
After 4 packs, Case full should light.
When the case is full, the belt should stop by itself.

scenarios.name: Case removed starts a new case

assertions.says: Case removed should put Case full out.
Case removed should set the packs back to 0.
Case removed should set the bottles back to 0.
After Case removed, Start should run the belt again.

scenarios.name: A stop part-way through keeps both counts

assertions.says: Nine bottles before Stop: 3 in the next pack.
With the belt stopped for 1 s, the case is full 1 s later.
The counts must carry on after a stop: the case is full by 13.8 s.
